# ThreadSanitizer runtime suppressions. Referenced from the TSan job's
# TSAN_OPTIONS in .github/workflows/asan.yml (same pattern as lsan.txt).
#
# Jolt's JPH_ENABLE_ASSERTS lock-ownership bookkeeping (vendored code, so we
# suppress rather than patch). JPH::Mutex / JPH::SharedMutex wrap the STL
# mutexes and, in assert builds only (the TSan job builds Debug), track the
# owning thread in an mLockedThreadID field as a best-effort recursive-lock
# detector. try_lock() reads that field in its assert BEFORE acquiring the
# mutex, racing unlock()'s clear of it (Jolt/Core/Mutex.h:126 vs :148, and the
# SharedMutex twins). The mutex itself synchronizes correctly — only the
# diagnostic field races. A true positive against the C++ memory model, benign
# on x86-64, shipped knowingly by upstream in assert builds (same verdict
# family as #350's allocator race). First seen: master Sanitizers run
# 31188714433, PhysicsJoint3DTest.PathPositionMotorSettlesAtTargetFraction —
# but any test that overlaps Jolt jobs with the stepping thread can trip it.
#
# File-based on purpose: it covers all six bookkeeping functions across both
# mutex classes, and a genuine engine-side race cannot have its RACING ACCESS
# inside this header — the only memory these inline wrappers themselves touch
# is the mutex's own bookkeeping field. Races merely *guarded* by Jolt mutexes
# still report normally (their racing frames are elsewhere).
race:Jolt/Core/Mutex.h

# ── More vendored-Jolt (v5.6.0) races in the same benign family ───────────────
# Surfaced once the TSan job could reach the test phase again: its vcpkg setup
# had been failing on a transient "socket hang up" ever since #773 (see the
# retry wrapper in .github/actions/setup-vcpkg), so the suite had not actually
# run under TSan in a long while and these went unseen. 134/5682 physics tests
# aborted here (halt_on_error=1); EVERY racing access reported is inside vendored
# Jolt — zero engine frames are the racing access. The physics tests pass under
# ASan+LSan and behaviourally on the same commit; only TSan flags Jolt's
# lock-free internals, which are known-noisy under TSan and shipped that way by
# upstream. These are pre-existing (also red on master / #773 / #784) and belong
# to the sanitizer/build config — added here to get the suite green again;
# worth a physics-owner sanity pass.
#
# SYMBOL-scoped, not file-scoped: each rule names exactly the reviewed race
# function, so any OTHER (as-yet-unseen) race in the same file still reports —
# the TSan audit path is preserved. This matters most for QuadTree.cpp, a large
# broadphase TU where a file rule would blanket real races too.
#
# JobSystem.h — Job's atomic refcount. A worker's AddRef() fetch_add (:194)
# races the main thread re-initialising that atomic when FixedSizeFreeList hands
# the SAME Job slot back out (Job::Job :293); Execute() (:239/:244) is the same
# recycled-slot overlap. Lock-free job recycling, benign on x86-64 — the same
# "true positive vs the C++ memory model, shipped knowingly by upstream" verdict
# as the Mutex race above.
race:JPH::JobSystem::Job::AddRef
race:JPH::JobSystem::Job::Execute
# Jolt's per-update linear scratch allocator, touched by those overlapping
# recycled jobs.
race:JPH::TempAllocatorImpl::Allocate
# ASSERT-BUILD-ONLY broadphase consistency check (the TSan job builds Debug) that
# walks tree nodes while a job mutates them. Diagnostic-only, same category as
# the Mutex bookkeeping field.
race:JPH::QuadTree::ValidateTree
# UVec4 SIMD int load in the same broadphase/job overlap.
race:JPH::UVec4::sLoadInt4

# ── Mesa's own driver threads (libgallium), not engine code ───────────────────
# Needed by the GPU-under-sanitizer nightly (gpu-sanitizers-amd.yml), which is
# the only job that runs TSan with a REAL GL context; the routed TSan job passes
# --olo-gl-backend=none and never loads a driver.
#
# radeonsi spawns its own worker threads ('OloEngin:gdrv0' and friends) and
# synchronises them internally. TSan cannot see that synchronisation, because
# libgallium is not instrumented -- so every allocation the driver makes on one
# of its threads and frees on the caller's looks like a race between calloc and
# free with no engine frame in either stack. Observed on a readback in
# PostProcessPropertyTests: both racing accesses inside libgallium-25.2.7,
# reached through the engine only as the caller.
#
# called_from_lib, not a race: rule, because the racing frames ARE the
# interceptors (free/calloc) and carry no symbol of their own. Scoped to the one
# library, so a genuine engine-side race still reports normally.
called_from_lib:libgallium

# ── Mesa's RADV Vulkan driver, same category as libgallium above ─────────────
# The libgallium rule's rationale ends "the routed TSan job passes
# --olo-gl-backend=none and never loads a driver". That stopped being true on
# 2026-09-12: ShaderCompileBudget.EveryComputeShaderBuildsOnTheRadvNullDeviceWithinBudget
# (9286bc412) brings up a RADV NULL DEVICE to compile every .comp, so the routed
# TSan job now does load a Vulkan driver — a different Mesa library from the GL
# one, so the existing rule does not cover it.
#
# RADV spawns its own disk-cache worker threads ('OloEngi:disk$0', 'disk$1') and
# synchronises them with a pthread_barrier it allocates on the CALLER's stack.
# libvulkan_radeon is not instrumented, so TSan cannot see that synchronisation
# and reports the teardown as a race:
#
#   Write of size 1 by thread T62:  pthread_barrier_destroy <- libvulkan_radeon.so+0x2a3860
#   Previous read      by thread T2: pthread_barrier_wait    <- libvulkan_radeon.so+0x2a479c
#   Location is stack of main thread.
#
# EVERY frame below the interceptor is <null> inside libvulkan_radeon; no engine
# frame is a racing access — the test appears only as the caller that brought the
# device up. Intermittent, because it needs the barrier teardown to overlap a
# still-waiting worker: PR #1291 hit it on TSan shard 4/4 while PR #1287 passed
# the same shard on the same test in the same window. With halt_on_error=1 one
# report aborts the whole ctest case, and it records NO gtest failure — the
# results XML is clean and only the job's exit code (8) shows it, which is what
# makes this one expensive to diagnose from the summary alone.
#
# called_from_lib, not a race: rule, for the same reason as libgallium: the
# racing frames ARE the interceptors (pthread_barrier_*) and carry no symbol of
# their own. Scoped to the one library, so a genuine engine-side race still
# reports normally.
called_from_lib:libvulkan_radeon
